newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's Turf Club profit after tax 0.32 mln punt.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Turf Club profit after tax 0.32 mln punt.

text.p: Ireland's Turf Club, which is responsible for the rules and for the day-to-day administration of horse racing, on Wednesday announced an operating profit after tax of 0.32 million Irish pounds.
The Turf Club said in a results statement that this compared with a 1995 loss of 0.10 million Irish pounds.

"1996 was the first year since 1991 that a profit was retained. Losses accumulated between 1992 and 1995 amounted to over 0.4 million punts and the 1996 profit will go some way towards recouping those losses," Michael Osborne, Senior Steward of the Turf Club, said.
The Turf Club said the return to profitability was due to an increase of 11 percent in racing administration income to 2.12 million Irish pounds.
It said this was due to an increase in bookage income because of higher entries to races and in income from registrations.

The Turf Club said racing administration expenses were maintained at 1995 levels despite the inclusion of a once-off cost associated with the transfer of the Equine Forensic Unit from Trinity College Dublin to BHP Laboratories in Limerick.

It said the transfer cost amounted to 0.08 million Irish pounds and represented the Turf Club's contribution towards the re-deployment of Trinity College staff who were exclusively employed in the Equine Forensic Unit for a long number of years and did not wish to relocate to Limerick.
The Turf Club said the losses at the racecourse and training grounds had been reduced and it said it was optimistic that it would return to profitability in 1997.
It said racing income was at its highest ever level in 1996 at 1.51 million Irish pounds, an increase of nine percent over 1995.
